claims.feature: other: fabricated fact in the record
claims.claim: Sato reports that AI-hallmarked obituaries that reached the top of Google Search announced the death of Brian Vastag, who was alive.
claims.source: Mia Sato, 'The unsettling scourge of obituary spam', The Verge, 12 Feb 2024
claims.quote: Except Brian Vastag was very much alive

claims.feature: other: fabricated fact in the record
claims.claim: Sato reports that the near-identical generated obituaries each repeated the same wrong statement of where the deceased had lived.
claims.quote: repeating inaccurate details, like where Mazur lived
claims.page: body, section on the Vastag/Mazur obituaries

claims.claim: Sato reports the generated obituary articles carry no quotations from family or friends of the deceased.
claims.quote: they lack quotes from family or friends of the deceased

claims.claim: Sato reports the generated obituary articles cite no outside reporting although they are written in the form of news articles.
A generated obituary of a Calgary woman, quoted by Sato as a demonstration passage, ends by advising the public to await verified information instead of stating a fact.
claims.source: a spam obituary quoted verbatim by Mia Sato, The Verge, 12 Feb 2024
claims.quote: the curious and concerned public is advised to stay tuned

claims.claim: Sato reports that one article announcing Vastag's death appears to be an AI summary of an op-ed he co-authored with the woman who had actually died.
claims.quote: appears to be an AI summary of the op-ed
claims.page: body, paragraph on hallmarks of AI generation

claims.claim: Weiss reports that Echovita's automated summary of a family-written obituary turned the dead woman's granddaughter into a grandson.
claims.source: Ben Weiss, 'The Morbid War Over Online Obituaries', WIRED, 26 Dec 2021

claims.claim: Weiss reports that the same automated summary left the dead woman's children out of the list of survivors.
claims.source: Ben Weiss, 'The Morbid War Over Online Obituaries', WIRED, 26 Dec 2021
claims.quote: her children weren’t mentioned as survivors

claims.claim: Weiss reports that the automated summary called the dead woman's two dogs her close friends without recording that they were dogs.
claims.source: Ben Weiss, 'The Morbid War Over Online Obituaries', WIRED, 26 Dec 2021
claims.quote: failing to note that they were dogs

claims.claim: Knibbs reports that MSN published an obituary of the former NBA player Brandon Hunter that was incoherent and oddly hostile.
claims.source: Kate Knibbs, 'The Bizarre Cottage Industry of YouTube Obituary Pirates', WIRED, 22 Sep 2023
claims.quote: an incoherent and oddly hostile obituary for former NBA player

claims.claim: Knibbs reports that critics assumed that garbled MSN obituary had been written by AI, and that Microsoft never confirmed it.
claims.quote: critics assumed the garbled article was written by AI

claims.claim: MyHeritage's amended terms, quoted by Russell, narrow the licence to use its records to personal, non-commercial and human use.
claims.source: MyHeritage terms and conditions, quoted by Judy G. Russell, 'AI meets TOS', The Legal Genealogist, 12 May 2026

claims.quote: easily generate lovely bios with lots of false

claims.quote: A single footnote meets current standards, but is clearly not enough
